sections.html:
Sumter County is older than almost any place a seller will meet. Residents 65 and up make up 57.6 percent of the population, and only 7.6 percent are under 18. The headcount reached an estimated 157,772 by mid-2025, a rise of 21.6 percent over the 2020 base of 129,752.

A household averages 1.93 people, and owners live in 87.6 percent of homes. The typical owned home is valued at $385,400, and owners paid a median $1,686 monthly with a mortgage against $602 without. Buyers here tend to ask hard questions about yearly carrying costs, so know your tax picture before you list. Permits totaled 3,516 in 2025, so a resale often sits next to new homes.

The appraiser values land and decides exemptions, while a separate collector sends the bills. The county's clerk of court also keeps the file for the Value Adjustment Board.

That board has five seats: two commissioners, one school board member, and two citizens, one named by each body. It hears appeals about value, classification and exemptions, leaves rates to the taxing authorities, and may not lower a value or give an exemption because of hardship. Qualified appraisers or attorneys serve as special magistrates, hear each petition and recommend a ruling.

Sumter follows the statewide calendar. January 1 fixes the assessment, March 1 closes homestead and classification filing, and April 1 is for personal property returns.

August brings the proposed-tax notice and a 25-day clock to petition. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own 30-day clock from the date the letter was mailed. Bills show up in November with a sliding discount of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent through February, and April 1 marks delinquency.

Yearly tax dates
WhenWhat to do
Mar. 1File for homestead
Aug.Proposed-tax notice arrives
25 days laterValue petition closes
Nov.Bills mailed, top discount
Apr. 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

Homestead reduces taxable value by as much as $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to school taxes and the rest does not. You must be living there on January 1, then apply on Form DR-501 at the appraiser's office.

After a sale the house is reassessed at market value, so the buyer's first full bill may far exceed yours. If you stay in Florida, you can carry up to $500,000 of capped difference to your next homestead if it is set up within three years, and Form DR-501T goes in with the application. Leaving the state forfeits it, because portability only links Florida homes.

sections.h2: Disputing a value without a lawyer
sections.html:
You can. The petition goes through the clerk, who also acts as clerk to the Value Adjustment Board, and a special magistrate hears the case. The magistrate is independent of the property appraiser, so you present evidence of value, such as recent comparable sales, repair estimates or errors in the property record.

The panel looks only at whether value, classification or exemption is right. A tight household budget does not move the outcome. If you have a contract pending, tell the title agent about any open petition so the closing statement handles the tax correctly.

sections.h2: Exemptions for older owners and service-connected disability
sections.html:
Many Sumter County sales touch age or military benefits. Counties and cities may adopt an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners over 65 with limited income, and a larger one equal to assessed value for 25-year residents whose home is worth under $250,000.

  • Older owners with a lasting service-connected disability: discount matching the VA rating.
  • Former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more disabled: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Total, permanent service-connected disability: possibly full relief on homestead.

Ask the Sumter County Property Appraiser which local ordinances add to this list and how a surviving spouse is treated.

sections.h2: The buyer's first bill versus yours
sections.html:
Expect a jump. You may have lived under the Save Our Homes limit, which holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change (2.7 percent for 2026). Once the deed records, the house is valued at market on the following January 1 and the limit starts over for the buyer.

A buyer who wants homestead also needs to apply by March 1, since the exemption is not automatic. Both sides gain from knowing this before closing, because the old bill on the listing sheet is a poor guide to the new one.

  • Your capped value does not transfer.
  • The buyer applies for homestead after taking title and living there on January 1.
  • If you move within Florida, you may port the savings.

sections.h2: What can cancel homestead before a sale
sections.html:
Three events end it: renting the home out, ceasing to use it as the permanent residence, or no longer being a Florida permanent resident.

If you move away before listing, speak with the appraiser about your status. One exception: a servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption. You and your listing agent should confirm the status before preparing the tax proration, and buyers should ask what exemptions the parcel carried last year.

Stamp tax is seventy cents for each hundred dollars of price. A mortgage the buyer takes over is added to the price.

Everyone on the deed is liable, so let the contract say who funds it. The clerk bills $5.00 on page one and $4.00 afterward, plus add-ons. A probated estate gets relief because a personal representative's deed is not taxable. A family deed made only for estate planning gets none.

sections.h2: Selling a house with unpaid tax
sections.html:
Overdue taxes become certificates sold by June 1, and a holder can seek a deed after two years. At the clerk's tax deed auction the winner leaves 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and pays the balance in 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.

Paying at closing avoids all of it, and a title company will normally insist on that anyway. A homestead parcel is further protected, since its opening bid in a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value. Request a payoff and a certificate search before you sign a contract.

With a cash buyer, the same steps apply, but there is no lender to wait on, so the payoff letter and title search set the closing date. Bring your deed, latest tax bill and any HOA or lien paperwork to the first meeting.

Because so many Sumter owners are retirees, buyers often arrive with cash from a prior home sale and ask for quick possession. That can shorten the timeline, but it does not shorten the paperwork: the clerk still has to record the deed, and the appraiser still has to move the exemption off your name. Ask your closing agent to confirm that the tax proration, any open petition and the payoff for earlier years are all on the settlement statement before you sign.

faqs.q: What share of Sumter County is 65 or older?
When is the Sumter County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: March 1, filed with the Sumter County Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Who hears assessment appeals in Sumter County?
faqs.a: The Value Adjustment Board, an independent five-member panel, with hearings run by special magistrates. The clerk serves as its clerk.

faqs.q: Can the board cut a Sumter County value for hardship?
faqs.a: No. It cannot change an assessed value or grant an exemption or classification based on personal hardship.

faqs.q: Does a Sumter County seller pay a deed tax?
faqs.a: Yes: seventy cents per $100 of price, owed at the clerk's counter. The contract decides which party actually pays, and every signer stays liable to the state regardless.
